title: N-Body simulation
summary: Advance the Jovian planets 1,000,000 steps with a symplectic integrator.
description: Classic five-body gravitational simulation (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game, advanced 1,000,000 steps of 0.01 with a symplectic integrator. Each iteration starts from slightly different initial conditions (planet positions scaled by 1 + (iteration mod 997) * 1e-5; iteration 0 is the classic setup). The energy before and after, rounded to 9 decimals, is the result.
pseudocode:
bodies = decode(instance)             # position, velocity, mass; untimed
start timer
offset sun velocity so total momentum = 0
e0 = energy(bodies)
repeat 1,000,000 times:
    for each pair (i, j) with i < j:
        d    = pos[i] - pos[j]
        mag  = 0.01 / |d|^3
        vel[i] -= d * mass[j] * mag
        vel[j] += d * mass[i] * mag
    for each body b: pos[b] += 0.01 * vel[b]
e1 = energy(bodies)
stop timer
hash round(e0 * 1e9), round(e1 * 1e9)
reveals: Scalar floating-point throughput, loop optimisation and (where the compiler can) auto-vectorisation.
caveat: Result depends on iteration count, precision and compiler math flags. We forbid fast-math and FMA contraction so every language must produce the identical 9-digit energies.
